chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'A man performed Dhahr with his wife but did not return (to her).' He said, 'Upon him is the expiation before they touch each other.' I said, 'But he had intercourse with her before he expiated.' He said, 'He did poorly.' I said, 'Is there something upon him?' He said, 'He must free a slave as well.'

key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation, the penalty required to lift the prohibition of Dhahr.
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Dhahr, a form of pre-Islamic and early Islamic divorce where a husband declares his back is like his mother's back, prohibiting intercourse but not ending the marriage.
key_terms.عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ: Freeing a slave, one of the stages of expiation for Dhahr.
key_terms.يَتَمَاسَّا: They touch each other, referring to sexual intercourse.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man has intercourse with his wife before expiating Dhahr?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific penalty for delaying the expiation (Kaffarah) of Dhahr until after consummation, distinguishing it from the standard ruling. The Imam characterizes this delay as 'Ihsan' (erring) and 'Zulm' (injustice), mandating the additional freeing of a slave as a compensatory act. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the pre-intercourse expiation is a strict condition to validate the release from the Dhahr state.
